Q: gprof produces empty output A:

I encountered the same problem with the latest MSYS2 with:

  • gcc.exe (Rev8, Built by MSYS2 project) 15.2.0
  • GNU gprof (GNU Binutils) 2.45.1

As already said, the solution is do add -no-pie. BUT if you have a compile and a linker steps: don't forget to add it not just to the compiler but also the linker options.

And if you building and linking one or multiple libraries and want to examine function calls there, those need the -pg -p -no-pie options as well. On the compiler and if they need linking themself, you need to add the options there too.

Q: Get unique elements in multiple List columns A:

If you want to stay inside Polars (avoiding to_list() and Python-side loops), you can do it entirely with expressions. You can just explode both columns, stack and then unique.

import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "a": [range(1, 3), range(5, 10)],
    "b": [range(4, 9), range(6, 11)],
})

unique_vals = (
    df
    .select(pl.all().explode()) 
    .melt(value_name="val")       
    .select(pl.col("val").unique())
    .to_series()
    .to_list()
)
# -> [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Or you can try Concatenate lists row-wise, explode, then unique.

unique_vals = (
    df
    .select(pl.concat_list("a", "b").alias("lists")) 
    .select(pl.col("lists").arr.explode().alias("val"))
    .select(pl.col("val").unique())
    .to_series()
    .to_list()
)

In reality, kindly keep in mind that staying in Polars (using explode, melt, and unique) is typically much faster and memory efficient than building Python lists and set-comprehensions, especially for large data sets. Hope it gives you clarity.

Updated my answer based on the comments.

select(pl.all().explode()) tries to explode each list column independently. Since column a has a total of 7 elements and column b has 10, Polars will not be able to maintain the DataFrame rectangulad. Exploded columns must produce the same number of rows when exploded together, otherwise you hit a shape mismatch.

Since melt is deprecated and I also have checked, kindly use unpivot.

import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "a": [range(1, 3), range(5, 10)],  
    "b": [range(4, 9), range(6, 11)], 
})

unique_vals = (
    df
    .unpivot(value_name="value") 
    .select(pl.col("value").arr.explode()) 
    .select(pl.col("value").unique())
    .to_series()
    .to_list()
)

print(unique_vals)  # -> [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

Q: Read binary file with R A:

Here is another approach using bmp:::ConvertIntToUInt() and readBin() directly for type coercion:

ConvertIntToUInt <- function(x, adjustment = 2^32) {
  x = as.numeric(x)
  signs = sign(x)
  x[signs < 0] = x[signs < 0] + adjustment
  x
}

# raw_vector <- readBin("filename.DAT", "raw", 10e6)

# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40673592/convert-hexadecimal-character-vector-to-raw-vector-in-r
hexchar_vector <- unlist(strsplit("44 5f 93 e8 34 e6 f1 a9 a1 10 35 2e b0 62 c5 7f b7 fd 61 c7 ef 37 a7 21 45 63 04 62 de 57 7b 99 7e 30 d3 ab cb 1c b9 69 d2 a6 c8 8e 88 ca 06 7a bb b1 7a dc 70 3f 13 1a 51 85 a9 68", split = " "))
integer_vector <- base::strtoi(hexchar_vector, base = 16L) # Convert strings to integers according to the given base using the C function strtol, or choose a suitable base following the C rules.
raw_vector <- base::as.raw(integer_vector) # Creates objects of type "raw" from integers.

raw_matrix <- matrix(raw_vector, nrow = 12)

var1 <- ConvertIntToUInt(readBin(raw_matrix[1:4,], what = "int", n = NCOL(raw_matrix), size = 4L, signed = TRUE, endian = "little"))
var2 <- readBin(raw_matrix[5:6,], what = "int", n = NCOL(raw_matrix), size = 2L, signed = FALSE, endian = "little")
var3to5 <- matrix(readBin(raw_matrix[7:12,], what = "int", n = NCOL(raw_matrix)*3, size = 2L, signed = TRUE, endian = "little"), ncol = 3L)
colnames(var3to5) <- c("var3", "var4", "var5")

df <- data.frame(var1 = var1, var2 = var2, var3to5)
